description: How modern cryptographic primitives are built, combined into protocols, and broken when used badly. In the lab students implement ciphers, hashes, signatures and key exchanges at toy scale, mount real attacks on flawed designs, and review the cryptography of a mobile-money style system.
modelledOn: Boneh and Shoup, A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography
Ferguson, Schneier and Kohno, Cryptography Engineering
Katz and Lindell, Introduction to Modern Cryptography
NIST Special Publications 800-57 and 800-131A (key management and algorithm transitions)
outcomes: State and use security definitions such as IND-CPA, IND-CCA and unforgeability, and reason about concrete security levels.
Implement and attack block-cipher modes, MACs, hashes and public-key schemes at toy parameters.
Select authenticated encryption, key exchange and signature schemes and justify their parameters.
Analyse an authentication or key-exchange protocol and find replay, reflection and man-in-the-middle attacks.
Identify and exploit common implementation failures such as nonce reuse, weak randomness and timing leaks.
Produce a cryptographic design review that maps controls to a threat model and to applicable standards and law.

units.title: Security definitions and mathematical toolkit
topics: Threat models, Kerckhoffs's principle, computational security and negligible functions
Security games: IND-CPA, IND-CCA2, EUF-CMA and PRF/PRP distinguishing advantage
Randomness: CSPRNGs, entropy sources, nonces versus IVs and the birthday bound
Number theory toolkit: modular arithmetic, extended Euclid, CRT, Fermat and Euler, Miller-Rabin primality testing
Reductions, concrete security and security levels in bits

units.title: Block and stream ciphers
topics: Feistel and substitution-permutation designs; AES rounds, GF(2^8) arithmetic and key schedule
Modes of operation: ECB, CBC, CTR and XTS; padding and why ECB leaks
Stream ciphers: LFSRs, RC4 biases, ChaCha20 and keystream reuse
Cryptanalysis: differential and linear cryptanalysis, meet-in-the-middle and double encryption
CBC malleability and padding-oracle attacks

units.title: Hash functions and MACs
topics: Preimage, second-preimage and collision resistance; birthday attacks; Merkle-Damgard and length extension
SHA-2 and the SHA-3 sponge construction
HMAC, CMAC and Poly1305; forgeries and constant-time tag comparison
Password hashing and key derivation: PBKDF2, bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2 and HKDF
Merkle trees, hash chains and commitments, with a mobile-money ledger as example

units.title: Public-key encryption and signatures
topics: RSA: key generation, textbook weaknesses, OAEP and PSS padding, small-exponent and common-modulus attacks
Discrete logarithm groups: Diffie-Hellman, ElGamal and generic attacks such as baby-step giant-step
Elliptic curves: group law, ECDH, X25519, ECDSA, EdDSA and the danger of nonce reuse
Digital signatures: security notions, hash-then-sign and Schnorr signatures
Post-quantum cryptography: the effect of Shor's algorithm, lattice-based key encapsulation and hash-based signatures
Hybrid encryption and the KEM/DEM paradigm

units.title: Key exchange and public-key infrastructure
topics: Authenticated key exchange, forward secrecy and ratcheting ideas
X.509 certificates, chains of trust, revocation (CRL, OCSP) and certificate transparency
Trust models and key management: trust on first use, HSMs, rotation and threshold secret sharing
The TLS 1.3 handshake and key schedule
Password-authenticated key exchange: SRP and the idea of OPAQUE

units.title: Authenticated encryption
topics: Composition: encrypt-then-MAC, MAC-then-encrypt and encrypt-and-MAC
AEAD interfaces and schemes: AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and CCM; associated data
Nonce misuse and misuse-resistant modes (SIV)
Encrypting stored data: disk and database encryption, format-preserving encryption and tokenisation of card numbers
Envelope encryption, key wrapping and cloud key management services

units.title: Cryptographic protocol design
topics: Building blocks: nonces, timestamps, challenge-response and replay protection
Classic protocol attacks: reflection, man-in-the-middle and the Needham-Schroeder public-key flaw
Formal analysis: symbolic models, attack traces and computational proofs
Zero-knowledge proofs: Schnorr identification, the Fiat-Shamir transform and commitments
Authentication in practice: HOTP and TOTP, end-to-end messaging, and PIN protection in USSD and SMS mobile-money flows
Secret sharing, threshold schemes and homomorphic tallying for e-voting

units.title: Common implementation failures
topics: Side channels: timing, cache and power; constant-time programming
Randomness failures: weak generators, repeated nonces and RSA keys sharing a prime (batch GCD)
API and design misuse: ECB, static IVs, hard-coded keys, homemade ciphers, downgrade attacks and compression oracles
Using high-level libraries and misuse-resistant APIs; crypto agility
Case studies of real failures: root cause through design, code and process
Auditing cryptographic code: known-answer tests, negative tests and fuzzing

units.title: Standards, review and project
topics: Threat model and primitive selection for a complete system
Parameter choice and the key lifecycle: generation, storage, rotation, revocation and destruction
Standards and law: NIST guidance, FIPS 140, PCI DSS and the Ghana Data Protection Act
Writing and presenting a cryptographic design review

schedule.title: Security games, randomness and number theory
schedule.exercise: Define IND-CPA with a game, compute a modular inverse and a CRT solution by hand, and estimate the sample size at which a 64-bit hash collides.

tasks.title: Compute modular inverses with extended Euclid, apply the Chinese remainder theorem to two congruences, and run Miller-Rabin on five numbers labelling primes and composites
Write a distinguishing game for a biased pseudorandom generator, run 10,000 trials, and estimate the adversary's advantage with a confidence interval
Find a collision in a 32-bit truncated hash by random sampling, measure the sample count over 100 runs, and compare it with the birthday-bound estimate

schedule.title: AES and modes of operation
schedule.exercise: Trace one AES round on a block, explain why ECB leaks structure, and show why reusing a keystream destroys confidentiality.

tasks.title: Implement AES SubBytes, ShiftRows and MixColumns on one block and check the round output against a published test vector
Encrypt a bitmap image with ECB and with CTR using a library, display both, and explain the leakage visible in the ECB result
Exploit keystream reuse: given two ciphertexts under the same stream-cipher key and nonce, recover both messages by crib dragging

schedule.title: Block-cipher cryptanalysis and padding oracles
schedule.exercise: Build a difference distribution table for a small S-box, count the work of a meet-in-the-middle attack, and explain the padding-oracle attack step by step.

tasks.title: Build a difference distribution table for a 4-bit S-box and identify the highest-probability differential an attacker would use
Implement a padding-oracle attack against a provided CBC decryption service and recover a 32-byte message byte by byte
Mount a meet-in-the-middle attack on double encryption with a toy 24-bit block cipher and compare the work with brute force on 48 bits

schedule.title: Hashes, MACs and password storage
schedule.exercise: Show the avalanche effect in SHA-256, explain why a secret-prefix MAC is forgeable, and pick password-hashing parameters for a 100 ms login budget.

tasks.title: Compute SHA-256 of small inputs, flip one input bit, and plot the number of changed output bits over 1000 trials to show the avalanche effect
Forge a tag for an appended message against a naive secret-prefix MAC using length extension, then show HMAC resists the same attack
Build a Merkle tree over eight mobile-money transactions, then produce and verify an inclusion proof for one of them
Compare PBKDF2, bcrypt and Argon2 cracking cost for a short password list at a stated hash rate, and choose parameters meeting a 100 ms login budget

schedule.title: RSA, discrete logarithms and elliptic curves
schedule.exercise: Generate a small RSA key and decrypt by CRT, solve a toy discrete logarithm, and add points on an elliptic curve.

tasks.title: Generate an RSA key from two 16-bit primes, encrypt and decrypt three messages with checked modular arithmetic, and verify the CRT shortcut
Run Diffie-Hellman in a small prime group, then recover the shared secret from the public values using baby-step giant-step and count the steps
Break RSA in three flawed setups: small public exponent without padding, two keys sharing a prime, and a common modulus, recovering the plaintext in each
Implement point addition and scalar multiplication on a small elliptic curve, then recover an ECDSA private key from two signatures that reuse a nonce

schedule.title: Signatures, post-quantum schemes and hybrid encryption
schedule.exercise: Sign and verify with Schnorr signatures, compare the sizes of classical and lattice-based keys, and build a hybrid encryption scheme.

tasks.title: Sign and verify three messages with Schnorr signatures in a small group, then show that a modified message fails verification
Build a hybrid encryption scheme with an ephemeral key exchange, key derivation and a symmetric cipher, and test it on a 1 MB file
Compare key and ciphertext sizes of RSA-2048, X25519 and a lattice-based KEM, and compute the extra bandwidth for 1 million handshakes a day on a mobile network

schedule.title: Key exchange, PKI and TLS
schedule.exercise: Show a man-in-the-middle on unauthenticated Diffie-Hellman, validate a certificate chain, and label the messages of a TLS 1.3 handshake.

tasks.title: Split a secret into five shares with threshold three using polynomial interpolation over a prime field, and reconstruct it from three different subsets
Run Diffie-Hellman with and without signed ephemeral keys, mount a man-in-the-middle in the first case, and show it fails in the second
Parse a certificate chain from provided files, verify each signature and validity date, and report which check fails when an intermediate is removed or expired
Trace a TLS 1.3 handshake capture, label each message and key-schedule stage, and work out which secrets a later theft of the server key would expose

schedule.title: Authenticated encryption and key management
schedule.exercise: Compare three ways of combining encryption and MACs, explain what happens when a GCM nonce repeats, and design envelope encryption for cloud storage.

tasks.title: Implement encrypt-then-MAC with AES-CTR and HMAC, and show that a flipped ciphertext bit is rejected before any decryption happens
Encrypt two messages under AES-GCM with a repeated nonce, recover the XOR of the plaintexts, then switch to a misuse-resistant mode and repeat the attempt
Design envelope encryption for a cloud bucket with per-object data keys wrapped by a master key, and test that rotation re-wraps keys without re-encrypting data

schedule.title: Protocol attacks and formal analysis
schedule.exercise: Break a naive challenge-response login by replay, run the man-in-the-middle on the Needham-Schroeder public-key protocol, and state the fix.

tasks.title: Add nonces and timestamps to a naive challenge-response login, replay a captured message to show the flaw, and verify the fix blocks it
Simulate the Needham-Schroeder public-key protocol with an intruder, execute the man-in-the-middle run, and implement the fix of adding the responder's identity
Model a small authentication protocol in a symbolic checker supplied with the task, find the attack trace, and repair the protocol until verification passes

schedule.title: Zero knowledge, one-time codes and mobile-money protocols
schedule.exercise: Prove knowledge of a discrete logarithm without revealing it, implement a one-time code generator, and review a USSD PIN flow for leaks.

tasks.title: Implement TOTP with HMAC-SHA1, generate codes for 10 time steps, and verify they match a provided test vector
Implement a Schnorr proof of knowledge made non-interactive with Fiat-Shamir, verify it, then show a cheating prover without the secret fails
Tally an e-voting scheme using additively homomorphic encryption with a toy Paillier key, and verify the total is correct without decrypting any single ballot
Review a USSD and SMS mobile-money PIN flow in a scenario, find where it leaks the PIN or allows replay, and propose a protocol that fixes both

schedule.title: Side channels, randomness and misuse
schedule.exercise: Recover a tag by timing, factor weak RSA keys with a batch GCD, and list the misuse errors in a small code sample.

tasks.title: Compute pairwise GCDs across 50 provided RSA public keys and factor every key that shares a prime factor with another
Time a naive comparison of MAC tags, recover a 4-byte tag byte by byte from timing differences, and fix it with constant-time comparison
Audit a provided small codebase using ECB, a static IV, a hard-coded key and a homemade XOR cipher, and rewrite it with an authenticated-encryption library

schedule.title: Libraries, case studies and testing cryptographic code
schedule.exercise: Replace low-level calls with a high-level library, write known-answer and negative tests, and analyse the root cause of one real-world failure.

tasks.title: Replace low-level primitives in a provided program with a high-level library's sealed-box and signature calls, and confirm old test messages still decrypt
Write known-answer and negative tests for an AES-GCM wrapper, including truncated tags and altered associated data, and fuzz it with 10,000 random inputs
Analyse a case study of a real key-generation or protocol failure in a scenario, trace the root cause through design, code and process, and write recommendations

schedule.title: Design review: choices, lifecycle and compliance
schedule.exercise: Write the cryptography section of a design review for a school-records or mobile-money system, justifying primitives, key sizes and key lifecycle against standards and law.

tasks.title: Map the encryption requirements of a payment standard and a data protection law to controls for a mobile-money app, and list the evidence an auditor would ask for
Select primitives, modes and key sizes for a school records system in a scenario, and justify each against its threat model and a 10-year protection requirement
Implement the key lifecycle of a small service covering generation, storage, rotation, revocation and destruction, with tests, and review it against a checklist
